name: intelligence-reference-set-v3-coverage
period_definition: Observation period = 7 consecutive UTC days starting at the window start (Tue 28 Jul 2026): 17 periods P01..P17, the last ending 2026-11-23. An incident belongs to the period containing its first_public_report_time (UTC); a record whose first report precedes the window start is 'pre_window'. Equal length, fixed boundaries, never re-cut per metric.
weekly_collection_basis: count of intelligence_events by collected_at (UTC date) and distinct source_id with >=1 report in the period; the 24 Nov partial day (751 reports) is outside the window.
zero_collection_days_basis: days in the window with fewer than 60 reports collected across all sources (generate_series left join; every other day in the window had >=139).
coverage_changes_source: intelligence/longitudinal_trends.py COVERAGE_CHANGES and KNOWN_BROKEN (imported by the baseline code; nothing duplicated here).

source_health_retention.note: intelligence_source_health holds no checks before 2026-10-25 (62 to 701 per source since), so per-source health cannot be reconstructed for earlier periods; earlier coverage is inferred from event first/last collection dates and registry created_at.

regulator_and_operator_sources_collectin.source: ATO Online Services / Practitioner Lodgment Service (6 feeds)

regulator_source_gap_effect: Across the whole window no collected report from ASIC, OAIC (after 10 Aug / 29 Aug), ATO, the Optus outage register or RBA exists; incident types whose first authoritative report comes from those sources were not observable by TJR in any period. This is a persistent source gap, NOT a per-week effect, so it cannot be removed by excluding weeks; it is listed per affected record (coverage_limits) and in the report.

other_source_start_dates.source: ARN - Australian IT Channel, iTnews, Google News x4
other_source_start_dates.note: added with the 6 Sep feed-ceiling step
no events before 19 Aug although registered 2026-06-12
